title: Task Brief authoring convention and Task Explorer
summary: Task Briefs explain task definitions with exact assistance and source boundaries; the Task Explorer composes current group and external catalogues. The rulebook owns authoring, and dated receipts below retain earlier inventory and validation counts.

decision_provenance: 2026-09-21 user answers: samples now and all tasks eventually; technically literate audience without specialist medical knowledge; existing and proposed tasks with clear draft marking. Other architecture and visual recommendations are by the assistant and await decisions. Later user response “all your rec” accepted shared definition briefs with case indexes, input-first reference reveals, reusable skill plus repository rulebook/template, and separately authoritative executable contracts. User subsequently requested searching and downloading necessary samples. This authorized bounded public data acquisition, not model trials. The user later requested complete brief coverage, then flagged repetitive badges, shared previews and metadata. The assistant refactored presentation to shared task rows with concise case differences and expandable provenance. The user then requested grouping repeated HealthAgentBench tasks and an equivalent AutoMedBench audit. The assistant consolidated dataset/target variants into shared navigation families while retaining individual contracts and source identities. The user explicitly requested further illustrations and authorized original SVG drawings where real examples cannot be downloaded. The assistant added labeled conceptual input/output pictures without treating them as native evidence. The user requested a final independent review and commit. Two read-only reviewers checked navigation and illustration semantics; the assistant fixed their findings, retained image selection captions and separated drawing code from navigation. On 2026-09-22 the user requested animated 3D illustrations for every task, inspired by OnCo Technologies. The assistant replaced the default conceptual infographic display with original procedural scenes, keeping source examples, exact contracts and reference reveals separately inspectable. The user then requested review and polish, simplification, cleanup and a focused commit. The assistant separated geometry from playback, corrected dimensionality and motion semantics, retained class labels without assigning an invented diagnosis, and added geometry and lifecycle regression checks. The user then found the shapes too abstract and requested shared assets with more organ detail. The assistant added 18 retained-source organ surfaces, authored brain/dental models, source-linked attribution, smooth shading and lighter multi-organ assemblies. The user then found the mixed wireframe and solid-mesh style incoherent and requested a consistent solution for all tasks. The assistant proposed and implemented shared shaded materials, information panels, semantic annotations and stable camera framing across the existing recipes, with a representative gallery for review; this does not record user acceptance of the specific design. The user requested a more elegant refinement because some models looked spiky and the animation looked cheap. The assistant refined shared geometry, added smooth GPU surface lighting with software fallbacks, and changed playback to one eased demonstration that settles on its output. This is an implementation for review, not user acceptance of its specific appearance.
reopen_when: When a source revision or task condition changes, a missing case inventory becomes available, or reader feedback demonstrates a needed format change.

decisions.decision: Selected Sculpted Atlas for the Task Explorer 3D teaching scenes and requested the refactor, independent tidy review, and commit.
